constraints.text: Replace the cover, keep the module

items.item: Dimensions, cover divisions and mechanical interfaces agree with the originating specification across the product and service images.
Changing fabric or arrangement preserves module identity and retains all connection hardware.
Named applications maintain the family sheet's Oat, Moss and Clay identities, common weave and corresponding cover seams.
Each furnished view and room plan reproduces its corresponding arrangement plate's module grouping, dimensions and gaps.
All room applications preserve the supplied boundary and openings and provide the required door-to-seating clearance.

requirementChecks.criteria: Read the original file properties: Format: presentation document; at least eight actual pages. Stage: final.

Where these components are visible or specified, the frame is 18 mm birch plywood with a clear water-based finish, the feet are solid smoked oak with hardwax oil, and connection hardware is black powder-coated steel. Hidden components need not be exposed in every image. Lighting variation is allowed; contradictory material labels or substitution of pale oak feet fail.

The overview identifies L as a left-arm chaise, S as armless and R as a right-arm seat, using front-view handedness, and supplies plan, front and side views. S retains separate cushions, rounded rectangular geometry, 40 mm corners, double stitching inset 15 mm and four square smoked-oak feet. Relevant detail views show 45 × 45 mm feet, independent cover divisions and underside interfaces; L and R have 620 mm arms integrated into their body covers. Drawing style may vary, but conflicting construction or handedness fails.

Each depicted state contains exactly one of each module, retaining four feet, two cushion inserts and three covers per module and the complete connection hardware. Rear edges align and joined upholstered edges touch without extra seam width. Ordinary occlusion is allowed; missing or duplicated modules, discarded hardware, or explicit inventory contradictions fail.

The family sheet pairs each of the three named swatches with its correct code and states the shared composition, 360 g/m² weight, 30°C gentle wash and air drying. Shared record labels are acceptable when their application to all three swatches is unambiguous. Swatches should reasonably represent the specified colours; photographic lighting need not reproduce hexadecimal values pixel for pixel. Missing, swapped or contradictory records fail.

The one-page source schedule establishes module dimensions and handedness, materials and finishes, connection locations and counts, service parts, cover divisions, all three fabric records and states A through C. It explicitly supplies 420 mm seat height, two assemblies per joined seam and 70% polyester, 30% cotton for downstream repetition. Records must agree with the client facts. Treat it as the originating specification; finished content alone does not prove export chronology.

The overview establishes the specified module envelopes, overall height, foot height, corner radius and stitching inset, and these features remain consistent in all four plates. Each target repeats the specification's 420 mm seat height. Arrangement dimensions show A at 2700 × 1600 mm and B/C at 3300 × 1600 mm including one 600 mm gap. A's geometry and seams remain unchanged between Oat and Moss. Viewpoint variation is acceptable; incompatible dimensions or changed profiles fail.

Each plate contains the same three module identities. Both A plates show joined L-S-R and four engaged assemblies. B identifies detached L with joined S-R; C identifies joined L-S with detached R. Each separated state accounts for two engaged and two parked assemblies retained beneath the modules. Insets or clear state diagrams may expose concealed hardware; confusing halves with complete assemblies or losing hardware fails.

Both sheets give two assemblies per seam at 250 mm and 650 mm from the rear. Joining is hand-operated. Cover service follows release, separation, cushion removal, cushion-cover removal, supported underside access, body-cover replacement, return upright, cushion-cover refitting and reconnection. Latch service shows supported access, exchange of latch and keeper halves, four M6 screws into retained inserts using a 4 mm hex key, then alignment and closing. Each half has two holes spaced 40 mm along the depth on a line 40 mm inward; latch halves belong on L/S right edges and keepers on S/R left edges. Clear combined steps are allowed; reversed interfaces or missing refitting fails.

Each application combines a furnished view with a dimensioned plan that agrees with its corresponding plate on module grouping, footprint, gaps and fabric. All use the supplied room's 7 m × 4 m boundary, 2.7 m clear height, door location and swing, and windows. Each plan dimensions an unobstructed door-to-seating route at least 900 mm wide. Furnishing and camera differences are acceptable; mismatched arrangements, moved openings or inadequate clearance fail.

Required image sheets carry RELAY, and the cover-service and family sheets also carry the complete cover message. The family swatch records govern Oat for A-before/B, Moss for A-after and Clay for C, including corresponding room scenes. Rendered fabrics retain the same weave and colour identity despite lighting differences. Wrong colour assignments or visibly different cover geometry fail; document copy and reuse are assessed separately.

The presentation has at least 10 pages, prints RELAY and the complete cover message, and repeats the source specification's 70% polyester, 30% cotton composition. Its statements about modules, arrangements, hardware and fabrics agree with the source records. Page layout may vary; insufficient pages, absent required text or contradictory facts fail.

Every listed earlier deliverable is recognizably reused within the presentation, covering specification, modules, arrangements, service, fabrics and room applications. Scaling, cropping and page composition are allowed when the source remains identifiable and its relevant content readable. Merely naming a deliverable or substituting unrelated new imagery does not count.

Review the entire 10-second video. It begins with joined L-S-R in A and ends with separate L and joined S-R in B, including the 600 mm gap. All three recognizable modules remain visible throughout without replacement, disappearance or duplication. The two assemblies at the L-S seam open and remain retained, changing the total from four engaged to two engaged plus two parked; the S-R pair stays joined. The specification's two assemblies per joined seam are clearly communicated. Editing style may vary if continuity and hardware states remain assessable.
